Consult Summary:
- Adult male with 5-day history of upper respiratory symptoms (dry cough, rhinorrhea, myalgias, intermittent headache/chills) consistent with a viral upper respiratory tract infection; examined via video with mild posterior oropharyngeal erythema and no signs of lower respiratory involvement — managed conservatively with symptomatic treatment and safety-netting.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Dry, hacking cough, runny nose, muscle aches, intermittent headache and chills for approximately five days (started at start of last weekend).
- Timeline/progression:
  - Symptoms began ~5 days ago and have persisted without reported worsening; described as a typical cold course.
- Exacerbating/relieving/initiating factors:
  - Has taken paracetamol and his regular medications; no other specific triggers or relievers documented.
  - Clinician recommended use of “Night Nurse/Day Nurse” preparations; noted compatible with current medications.
- Associated symptoms / review of systems:
  - Cough: described primarily dry/hacking.
  - Rhinorrhea: present.
  - Myalgias, occasional headache, subjective chills: present.
  - Sputum: conflict in transcript — patient initially said “yeah” to producing phlegm then immediately clarified it is a dry cough (conflict noted).
  - Hemoptysis: denied/not reported.
  - Shortness of breath/wheeze: denied.
  - Neck glands/lymphadenopathy: patient reports none on self-exam.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No shortness of breath, no wheeze or rattly chest sounds reported, no fever measurement recorded, no chest pain.

Past Medical History:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus: diagnosed approximately 5–6 years ago.
  - Patient monitors blood glucose at home; reports readings “no issues” / “within normal range.”
  - Medication: metformin — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Hypertension (described as “slight blood pressure”):
  - Medication: lisinopril — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Other chronic conditions: none mentioned.
- Current regular medications: metformin, lisinopril (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Acute/PRN medications taken for current illness: paracetamol — dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- Not documented.

Social History:
- Location confirmed to be private for confidential consultation.
- No information provided about smoking, alcohol, or recreational drug use.
- No work, travel, living situation, or other social details provided.

Family History:
- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: none documented (patient reported taking blood pressure this morning but could not recall reading; stated it was within normal range).
- General / HEENT:
  - Posterior oropharynx: mild redness (erythema) at the back of the throat.
  - Tonsils: not enlarged.
  - Neck: no palpable lymphadenopathy reported by patient.
- Respiratory:
  - No reported wheeze or rattles on history; no shortness of breath.
- Other exam findings: none documented.

Investigations:
- No imaging, labs, or diagnostic tests performed or reported during this consultation.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute viral upper respiratory tract infection (presumed viral common cold)
  - Assessment: Presentation and oropharyngeal findings consistent with viral infection; no signs of lower respiratory tract involvement on history/exam.
  - Plan:
    - Conservative symptomatic management (no antibiotic prescribed).
    - Analgesia/antipyretic already used: paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Recommended use of OTC symptomatic preparations referred to as “Night Nurse/Day Nurse” — dose/route/frequency not documented; clinician stated these are compatible with patient’s current medications.
    - Safety-netting: seek re-evaluation if any of the following occur — new or worsening shortness of breath, onset of wheeze, clinical deterioration, or if symptoms persist beyond three weeks.
- Issue 2: Type 2 diabetes mellitus — stable monitoring
  - Assessment: Patient self-monitors blood glucose and reports readings within his usual range at present.
  - Plan:
    - Continue current diabetes management (metformin) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
    - Continue home glucose monitoring as per usual; no changes recommended during this consultation.
- Issue 3: Hypertension — stable on current therapy
  - Assessment: Patient on lisinopril; reported recent blood pressure this morning described as within normal range but numerical value not provided.
  - Plan:
    - Continue lisinopril — dose/route/frequency not documented.
    - No further BP management changes recommended during this consultation.
- General plan items:
  - No prescriptions issued at this time.
  - Advise re-contact or in-person assessment if symptoms worsen, develop respiratory compromise, or persist beyond three weeks.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Allergies/intolerances: not documented.
  - Comprehensive medication list with doses, routes, frequencies: incomplete (metformin, lisinopril, paracetamol listed without dosing details).
  - Objective vitals: temperature, pulse, respiratory rate, blood pressure (numeric), oxygen saturation not documented.
  - Full respiratory examination findings (auscultation) and temperature measurement not documented.
  - No diagnostic testing performed (e.g., pulse oximetry, chest auscultation by clinician not documented).
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Sputum production: patient initially said “yeah” when asked about phlegm, then immediately corrected to state it is a dry cough — conflict noted.
- Transcript quality comment:
  - Audio/transcript adequate for clinical content; occasional pauses/filler words present but key clinical details were discernible.
